slides.title: YOUR MISSION
slides.relevance: In your B1 PET test, you'll need to listen for specific details in interviews. This lesson prepares you for that.

slides.title: DIGITAL TRUTHS
slides.question: Fact or Fiction: 70% of teens trust YouTubers more than traditional celebrities?

slides.title: THE VERDICT
slides.evidence: Research by Google/Ipsos shows that 70% of teenage YouTube subscribers say they relate to YouTube creators more than traditional celebrities.
slides.explanation: Online personalities often feel more authentic and relatable to younger audiences than distant movie stars.

slides.title: BARRIER REMOVAL
slides.content: We are going to learn 5 key words to help us understand the podcast.

slides.thai: ช่องว่างระหว่างวัย
slides.context_sentence: The generation gap makes it hard for my grandma to understand TikTok.

slides.title: TOM'S WORLD PODCAST
slides.instruction: Listen for the MAIN TOPIC and Dr. Schmidt's JOB.

slides.title: EX 1: MAIN TOPIC
slides.evidence: [Line 3] Today I’m looking at family life – specifically at teens and whether or not teenagers and their parents can ever really understand each other.
slides.explanation: Tom explicitly states he is looking at the relationship between teens and parents.

slides.title: EX 2: DR. SCHMIDT'S JOB
slides.evidence: [Line 7] I’m here today with psychologist Doctor Lisa Schmidt...
slides.explanation: Tom introduces her using her professional title.

slides.title: EXAM STRATEGY: MCQ
slides.content: Read the questions carefully before you listen. Look for keywords!

slides.title: DETECTION MISSION
slides.instruction: Listen and choose the correct option (Ex 3).

slides.title: EX 3: QUESTION 1
slides.evidence: [Dr. Schmidt] ...but my own research shows that there’s more to the story.
slides.explanation: She agrees online personalities are important but notes her research adds a different perspective.

slides.title: EX 3: QUESTION 2
slides.evidence: [Tom] ...if my mom tried to tell me what to wear ... [Dr. Schmidt] ...for questions of clothes and style, of course teens turn to the internet a lot.
slides.explanation: They agree that for style, the internet is the primary influence.

slides.title: EX 3: QUESTION 3
slides.evidence: [Tom] ...we talk about it a lot – because they’re going to pay for it.
slides.explanation: Tom admits discussing university with parents because of the financial support.

slides.title: EX 3: QUESTION 4
slides.evidence: [Dr. Schmidt] ...when it comes to some big things in life – career choice, education, finance, health and well-being – parents actually still have a lot of influence...
slides.explanation: The research lists these specific areas where parents remain influential.

slides.title: EX 3: QUESTION 5
slides.evidence: [Dr. Schmidt] Everyone’s always ready to say that the generation gap means parents and teens simply can’t communicate...
slides.explanation: She observes that the common perception is a complete lack of communication.

slides.title: YOUR TURN
slides.content: Discuss the four big areas with your partner. Who do you listen to?
